DMA Controller

This document defines the MC68450 direct-memory-access subsystem. Return to the main page.

Revision 1.1 adds the BIOS backup SRAM completion on U_DTACK_C pin 4, following memory map 2.3. The ownership gates exclude slot 13 from DMA; BIOS channel validation must reject the entire $FA0000-$FBFFFF range, including its mirror. See BIOS Backup SRAM. Revision 1.0 added four physical DMA channels for IDE, floppy, and two expansion slots. An idle expansion channel can be borrowed for a memory copy. The design shares the MC68EC000 bus, uses physical supervisor DRAM addresses, and keeps all channel programming inside the BIOS.

1. Purpose and Limits

The MC68450 moves words between physical DRAM and IDE, bytes between physical DRAM and the floppy controller or an expansion card, and words between two physical DRAM ranges. It is the only added bus master. Expansion cards can request a motherboard channel but cannot drive the address or function-code buses and cannot claim the bus.

Device transfers use single-address mode. The DMAC addresses DRAM while ACKx_n selects the device. Memory copies use M68000-compatible dual-address mode. The ATA connector's DMARQ and DMACK_n remain unused because this is not ATA multiword DMA or UDMA.

DMA cannot target VGA, ROM, I/O registers, the page-table aperture, or the paging control block, and the hardware says so rather than the firmware. Both I/O decoders take an ownership enable, the page unit closes its aperture while OWN_n is low, and U_PROT asserts a bus error for any DMA address at or above $400000. BIOS range checks come first, but a firmware mistake now aborts a channel instead of rewriting a page table. Physical addresses below $020000 are BIOS-private and include the vector table. The boot-ROM alias also takes the ownership term, so the MC68450 sees physical DRAM there whether or not the overlay is enabled.

2. Architecture

                         +---------------- MC68EC000
                         | BR/BG/BGACK
                         | A1..A23, FC, AS, DS, R/W
                         v
device REQ/PCL ----> MC68450L8 ---- ACK/DTC/DONE ----> device glue
                         |
 A8/D0..A23/D15 --------+--> 2 x ACT373 ----> A8..A23
                         +<-> 2 x HCT245 <-> D0..D15
 D15..D8 <------------- HCT245 HIBYTE -------------> D7..D0

motherboard DTACK --> HCT125 --> DMAC DTACK pin --> HCT125 --> tree
BUS_BERR_n --------> retained DMA fault -----------> BEC2..BEC0
RESET_n/PERIPH_RESET_n ----------------------------> BEC reset code
IRQ ------------------------------------------------> level 1 autovector

OWN_n is the master-select signal. Low enables the DMAC address latches and marks DMA ownership. CPU-side decode and the DMAC register chip select require OWN_n high.

3. Controller and Pin Use

Fit an MC68450L8 64-pin ceramic DIP in a machined-pin socket. The L8 part is rated for 2 MHz through 8 MHz and 0 C through 70 C. Record the mask code and full package marking in the build log. Apply every A84G restriction until a later mask is identified and supported by its own manufacturer documentation.

MC68450L8 groups and assigned connections
Pins Signals Connection
1..8 REQ3..REQ0, PCL3..PCL0 Expansion 2, expansion 1, floppy, IDE handshakes
9..15 BGACK_n, DTC_n, DTACK_n, UDS_n, LDS_n, AS_n, R/W Shared-bus and isolation logic
16, 18, 49, 51 Ground and +5 V Both supply pairs bypassed at the socket
17, 19, 20, 21, 22 CS_n, CLK, IACK_n, IRQ_n, DONE_n Register decode, DMA clock, +5 V tie, level 1, shared completion
23..29 ACK3_n..ACK0_n, BEC2..BEC0 Device glue and exception encoder
30..32 FC2..FC0 Shared function-code bus
33..48 A23/D15..A8/D0 Address latches and data transceivers
50, 52..57 A7..A1 Shared lower address bus
58..64 BG_n, BR_n, OWN_n, UAS_n, HIBYTE_n, DBEN_n, DDIR Arbitration and demultiplex controls

Tie IACK_n high. The motherboard supplies the autovector, so NIVR and EIVR are not used and retain their documented reset value of $0F unless diagnostic firmware reads them.

4. DMA Clock

U_DMA_MOD3 and U_DMA_TOGGLE are SN74F74N packages. U_DMA_NOR is an SN74F02N. The two state bits follow 00, 01, 10, 00; state 11 returns to 00 on the next master-clock edge. 

D(Q1) = NOT (Q1 OR /Q0)
D(Q0) = NOT (Q1 OR Q0)

00 -> 01 -> 10 -> 00
11 ----------------> 00

Q1 rising edge -> toggle flip-flop D=/Q
DMA_CLK_RAW = toggle Q = MASTER_CLK_40 / 6
Divider package allocation
Package Pins Use
U_DMA_MOD3, F74 1=/CLR0, 2=D0, 3=CLK0, 4=/PRE0, 5=Q0, 6=/Q0 Both asynchronous inputs high; pin 3 receives MASTER_CLK_40
U_DMA_MOD3, F74 8=/Q1, 9=Q1, 10=/PRE1, 11=CLK1, 12=D1, 13=/CLR1 Both asynchronous inputs high; pin 11 also receives MASTER_CLK_40
U_DMA_TOGGLE, F74 1=/CLR, 2=D, 3=CLK, 4=/PRE, 5=Q, 6=/Q Pin 2 to pin 6, pin 3 to Q1, pin 5 is DMA_CLK_RAW
U_DMA_TOGGLE, F74 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13 Unused: /PRE and /CLR high, D and CLK low, Q outputs open
U_DMA_NOR, F02 1,2->3 and 4,5->6 Q1,Q0 make D0; Q1,/Q0 make D1
U_DMA_NOR, F02 9,10->8 and 12,13->11 Unused inputs low; outputs open

Pin 8 of U_IO_CLK_BUF, a CD74ACT244E, takes DMA_CLK_RAW; pin 12 drives DMA_CLK. The first bank's existing active-low enable remains grounded. Outputs 18, 16, and 14 remain IO_CLK_ROOT, PIT_CLK, and TIMEOUT_CLK. Four channels remain spare.

At +100 ppm, DMA_CLK is 6.66733 MHz and its period is 149.985 ns. Each raw phase spans three master periods. Using the ACT244 2.4 ns minimum and 9.6 ns maximum propagation limits, the conservative shorter buffered phase is 75.0 - 7.2 = 67.8 ns before board skew and jitter. That leaves 12.8 ns over the MC68450L8 55 ns minimum. Allocate at most 5 ns to clock trace skew, oscillator jitter, and load-dependent distortion; verify both phases at pin 19.

The feedback path has a conservative 9.2 ns F74 clock-to-Q plus 6.5 ns F02 delay. Against the 24.9975 ns shortest master period and 4 ns F74 setup time, the pre-layout margin is 5.3 ns. Keep both feedback gates and the state package adjacent and hold total clock-to-D route skew below 2 ns. The divider has no reset connection. Its illegal state recovers and the output continues toggling while BEC reset is active.

5. Address and Data Demultiplexing

This circuit follows MC68450 manual Figure 2-2. Two CD74ACT373E transparent latches capture A8 through A23. Two SN74HCT245N transceivers carry D0 through D15. A third HCT245 crosses the upper and lower bytes for single-address transfers to 8-bit devices.

Demultiplex controls
Part Ports Control
U_DMA_A8_15, ACT373 D0..D7 from DMAC A8/D0..A15/D7; Q0..Q7 to bus A8..A15 LE pin 11 = NOT UAS_n; /OE pin 1 = OWN_n
U_DMA_A16_23, ACT373 D0..D7 from DMAC A16/D8..A23/D15; Q0..Q7 to bus A16..A23 Same LE and /OE controls
U_DMA_DLO, HCT245 A port at DMAC D0..D7, B port at system D0..D7 /OE pin 19 = DBEN_n; DIR pin 1 = DDIR
U_DMA_DHI, HCT245 A port at DMAC D8..D15, B port at system D8..D15 Same /OE and DIR controls
U_DMA_HIBYTE, HCT245 A port at system D8..D15, B port at system D0..D7 /OE = HIBYTE_n; DIR = R/W

A high HCT245 DIR transfers A to B. Thus DDIR high sends DMAC data to the system bus. On an even memory read to an 8-bit device, R/W high sends D15..D8 to D7..D0. On an even device-to-memory write, R/W low sends D7..D0 to D15..D8. Odd-byte cycles leave HIBYTE inactive.

U_DMA_UAS_INV is an SN74HCT04N. Gate 1 converts active-low UAS to the active-high ACT373 latch enable. Gate 2 produces OWN_ACTIVE, the inverted OWN_n used by the DTACK isolation buffer, the DMAC chip-select term, the high-half I/O decoder, and the boot-ROM alias gate. Ground the four unused inputs and leave their outputs open. OWN is already the required active-low output enable for the latches. Pull-ups keep UAS, DBEN, DDIR, and HIBYTE inactive while the MC68450 pins are high impedance.

6. Bus Arbitration

  1. The DMAC pulls processor BR_n low.
  2. The processor finishes its current cycle, releases its bus outputs, and pulls BG_n low.
  3. The DMAC waits for CS, IACK, AS, and BGACK to be inactive. It then pulls OWN_n low.
  4. One half DMA clock later it pulls BGACK_n low. Its first S0 drives FC, A1..A7, and the multiplexed upper address.
  5. After the last cycle it releases BGACK. It releases OWN one half DMA clock later. The processor synchronizes released BGACK before driving the bus.

The CPU and DMA clock patterns repeat every twelve 40 MHz periods, but startup phase is arbitrary. No cross-clock setup assumption is used. Both devices apply their documented asynchronous-input synchronizers. Reduced 2.2 kohm pull-ups make BR and BGACK rise to the 2.0 V input threshold in about 27 ns for a conservative 30 pF net, leaving the remaining latency to the receiver synchronizers.

The manual's 12-clock REQ-to-BGACK value is a minimum, or 1.8 us at nominal clock. It is not a service bound. The board-level bound adds the current CPU cycle, asynchronous phase, bus release, any in-flight DMA operand, DRAM refresh, and device READY delay as section 17 calculates.

7. Register Window and Chip Select

DS_ACTIVE   = NOT (UDS_n AND LDS_n)
CPU_OWNER  = OWN_n
DMAC_CS_n  = IO12_n OR (NOT CPU_OWNER) OR (NOT DS_ACTIVE)

Build the equation with HCT08/HCT32 gates. A DMA address in slot 12 cannot select the DMAC because OWN_n is low. A CPU byte or word access supplies A1..A7 and UDS/LDS as the manual requires. A16..A8 are not decoded, so the 256-byte block mirrors through the 128 KiB slot. Firmware uses the canonical block at $F80000-$F800FF.

Canonical register addresses for channel c
Offset Register Access
c+$00/$01 CSR/CER Separate bytes or one word; CSR is write-one-to-clear
c+$04..$07 DCR, OCR, SCR, CCR Bytes; SCR and CCR must never be one word write
c+$0A MTCR Word
c+$0C MAR Long word, even aligned
c+$14 DAR Long word, even aligned
c+$1A BTCR Word
c+$1C BAR Long word, even aligned
c+$25/$27 NIVR/EIVR Bytes; unused here
c+$29/$2D/$31/$39 MFCR, CPR, DFCR, BFCR Bytes
$FF GCR Global byte register

Channel bases are $00, $40, $80, and $C0. Reset clears CPR, DCR, OCR, SCR, CCR, CER, and GCR; sets NIVR and EIVR to $0F; sets CSR to $00 or $01 from PCL; and leaves the address, count, and function-code values unknown or unaffected as manual Table 3-1 states.

8. DTACK Isolation and Completion

Do not join the bidirectional DMAC DTACK pin to the motherboard's totem-pole completion output. U_DMA_DTACK_ISO is an SN74HCT125N with two independent paths.

SN74HCT125N isolation wiring
Gate Pins Function
1 /OE 1=OWN_n, A 2=DTACK_TO_DMA_n, Y 3=DMAC pin 11 Enabled only while DMA owns the bus
2 /OE 4=NOT OWN_n, A 5=DMAC pin 11, Y 6=DMAC_DTACK_n Enabled only for CPU register cycles
3 and 4 /OE pins 9 and 12 high; A pins 10 and 13 low; outputs 8 and 11 open Unused channels fixed

A 2.2 kohm pull-up at DMAC pin 11 provides the high level required by its open-drain MPU-mode DTACK output. A 4.7 kohm pull-up on DMAC_DTACK_n keeps the completion-tree input inactive while gate 2 is disabled. With 30 pF at that isolated node, reaching 2.0 V from 0.5 V takes 57 ns. Gate 2 remains enabled until OWN falls, after the CPU has released the cycle, so this RC does not extend a live register cycle. 

DTACK_GROUP3_n = IDE_DTACK_n AND DMAC_DTACK_n AND BSRAM_DTACK_n AND 1
DTACK_RAW_n    = GROUP0_n AND GROUP1_n AND GROUP2_n AND GROUP3_n
DTACK_n        = DTACK_RAW_n OR TIMEOUT_ACTIVE
DTACK_TO_DMA_n = DTACK_n OR DMA_FAULT

Add U_DTACK_C, an SN74F21N. Gate 1 uses pins 1, 2, 4, and 5 for IDE, DMAC, BSRAM_DTACK_n, and +5 V; pin 6 drives group 3. Tie unused gate-2 inputs 9, 10, 12, and 13 high and leave pin 8 open. The existing final F21 gate now takes groups 0 through 3. IDE gains one F21 level. The DMAC register path is HCT125, F21, F21, then F32.

The published maximums give 25 ns for the HCT125 path and 7 ns per F21 plus 8.5 ns for the F32, or 47.5 ns before routes and loading. This fits the CPU's 110 ns DTACK-release allowance with 62.5 ns for the source release, routing, and load. The DRAM path remains two F21 levels plus F32, 22.5 ns from its local completion source before routing; the former 28.5 ns budget remains conservative after the added group is wired with one FAST load per output.

The timeout counter clears whenever shared AS_n is high. It therefore restarts for every CPU or DMA bus cycle, including two halves of a dual-address operand. Bus ownership alone never advances a cumulative timeout. Verify at least 55 ns of counter reset between adjacent masters and cycles; the DMAC manual supplies at least one full high phase between its AS assertions.

9. Bus Exceptions and Reset

Rename the protection PAL output BUS_BERR_n. It combines timeout, interrupt-acknowledge, page, and protection faults, plus the DMA_BERR range test that fires on any DMA address at or above $400000. CPU_BERR_n = BUS_BERR_n OR (NOT OWN_n), so a DMA fault cannot signal the processor directly. The internal PAL term PROT_BERR remains internal and is not a board net.

An HCT32 gate forms DMA_FAULT_SET_n = BUS_BERR_n OR BGACK_n. Its low level asynchronously presets U_DMA_FAULT, one HCT74 half. The latch clears only after shared AS has returned high following DMAC termination. DMA_FAULT masks DTACK_TO_DMA_n high and drives the bus-error BEC code until the controller releases the failed cycle. A second HCT74 stage clocked by DMA_CLK records that the fault remained present for two rising edges before clear is allowed. This prevents a short source pulse from violating the BEC debouncer. 

DMA_RESET_n = RESET_n AND PERIPH_RESET_n

if DMA_RESET_n = 0: BEC2..BEC0 = 000
else if DMA_FAULT = 1: BEC2..BEC0 = 101 (H L H, bus error)
else: BEC2..BEC0 = 111 (normal)

clear DMA_FAULT only when AS_n=1 AND FAULT_SEEN_TWICE=1

Implement the equations with U_DMA_BEC, the spare PALCE16V8Q-15JC/4, and the two HCT74 fault stages. Reset has combinational priority and is independent of OWN and BGACK. Board reset therefore reaches BEC while the CPU owns the bus. CPU-generated peripheral reset also resets the DMAC. DMA_CLK is not reset or gated, so the DMAC can recognize both reset sources.

Power-on BEC reset remains asserted for the board's 100 ms reset interval. A warm peripheral reset remains asserted for at least ten DMA clocks, or 1.50 us. The existing CPU RESET-instruction pulse is longer than this. Bus-error sources either precede a possible DTACK or, for timeout, occur only because DTACK is absent. The fault latch masks later DTACK immediately. This satisfies the 50 ns BEC-before-DTACK rule without accepting a normal completion after a recorded fault.

The design emits no external halt, retry, relinquish-and-retry, or undefined BEC code. Descriptor-fetch and data faults use the same bus-error path. The DMAC suppresses DTC, leaves the current operand counters unadvanced, aborts that channel, and reports the register class in CER.

10. Level-1 Interrupt

DMAC IRQ_n is open drain. A 2.2 kohm pull-up feeds the level-1 input of U_IPL_ENC. Extend the autovector equation to include IACK_L1. A level-1 CPU-space acknowledge asserts VPA and returns autovector 25 from address $000064; it never asserts DMAC IACK.

The handler polls all four CSR values, snapshots CSR and CER before clearing them, processes every completion and error, and repeats until IRQ releases. CSR status is write-one-to-clear. An error kills the recorded channel owner, not whichever process happens to be current. BIOS-owned failures are fatal system errors.

11. Channels and Scheduling

Fixed channel allocation
Channel Use Priority Interface
0 IDE 1 ACK0, PCL0 READY, internal maximum-rate requests
1 Floppy 0, highest DRQ through REQ1, ACK1/DACK, DTC+DONE terminal count
2 Expansion slot 1 2 REQ2, ACK2, PCL2 READY
3 Expansion slot 2 2 REQ3, ACK3, PCL3 READY

Priority zero is highest in the MC68450. Equal-priority expansion channels use the controller's round-robin rule. IDE and expansion operations are capped at 32 operands per channel activation. This returns the bus between chunks and bounds CPU denial. Floppy retains highest priority because its FIFO has a hard service deadline.

A memory copy borrows an expansion channel under a BIOS lock. The slot's driver holds the lock whenever it may raise a request, so a borrow can only happen while that card is quiescent. Taking the lock without that rule would leave a card requesting service on a channel that has been reprogrammed for a memory copy, and the card would starve its own FIFO without any error being reported. The copy sets priority 3, programs a complete dual-address configuration, and restores the slot's configuration before releasing both the channel and the lock. With neither lock available the BIOS copies on the processor.

12. IDE Channel 0

Channel 0 uses a 16-bit, implicitly addressed device with ACK and READY. REQ0 is held inactive through 4.7 kohms and request generation is internal maximum rate. Firmware starts no more than 32 words after checking ATA BSY, DRQ, DF, and ERR for the current data phase.

CD74ACT157E U_IDE_DA_MUX selects CPU A3..A1 when ACK0 is high and selects three grounded inputs when ACK0 is low. Its common A/B select pin 1 receives ACK0_n and /G pin 15 is grounded. The three address outputs feed the existing HCT244 cable buffer. During DMA, ATA DA2..DA0 are driven 000, CS0 is active, and CS1 remains high. The fourth channel carries the PCL0 source and takes the same select.

Cross ATA DD7..DD0 to system D15..D8 and ATA DD15..DD8 to system D7..D0. Cross the byte enables with the lanes. Task-file and control bytes therefore use even addresses and UDS. PIO sector transfers no longer swap every data word. ATA string fields, IDENTIFY numeric fields, and ATAPI packets each follow their format-specific parsing rules. 

PIO_READ       = PIO_CYCLE AND R/W
PIO_WRITE      = PIO_CYCLE AND NOT R/W
DMA_DEV_READ   = DMA_CYCLE AND NOT R/W
DMA_DEV_WRITE  = DMA_CYCLE AND R/W

IDE_DIOR_n     = NOT ((PIO_READ OR DMA_DEV_READ) AND IDE_QB)
IDE_DIOW_RAW_n = NOT ((PIO_WRITE OR DMA_DEV_WRITE) AND IDE_QB)
IDE_DIOW_n     = IDE_DIOW_RAW_n OR (NOT ACK0_n AND NOT DTC_n)
IDE_BUF_DIR    = (ACK0_n AND R/W) OR (NOT ACK0_n AND NOT R/W)

IDE_PCL_MUX = NOT (IDE_QE AND IORDY), while ACK0_n=0
IDE_PCL_MUX = DTACK_n,                while ACK0_n=1
PCL0_n      = IDE_PCL_MUX OR BGACK_n

Replace the sequencer's QD PAL input with QE. QE cannot assert until four complete 5 MHz intervals after the first sampling edge, at least 799.92 ns at +100 ppm. QB starts DIOR or DIOW only after address selection has settled. Device-to-memory DIOR starts from ACK0 without waiting for UDS, then PCL0 permits the delayed DRAM write after ATA data is valid. Memory-to-device DIOW ends when successful DTC asserts, while DRAM data is still valid. A bus error suppresses DTC and ATA command recovery resets or drains the failed command before reuse. BGACK_n holds PCL0 inactive during CPU ownership, so only DMAC cycles reach the PCL input. All eight PAL macrocells are allocated, so an HCT08, an HCT32, and the spare HCT04 inverters carry READY, the DIOW trailing edge, drive reset, and the PCL0 gate. The equations, pin budget, and product-term counts are in IDE Interface.

IDE_DTACK stays high during ACK0. DRAM supplies completion. During a descriptor fetch, ACK0 is high and PCL0 follows motherboard DTACK as manual Figure 4-12 requires. The warning on p. 4-16 is about DTACK, not READY: if DTACK reached the controller before PCL0 on a device-to-memory transfer, the cycle would terminate without ever asserting the data strobes. It cannot happen here, because the DRAM request detector starts on those data strobes, so its DTACK always follows them.

13. Floppy Channel 1

Configure channel 1 for an 8-bit implicitly addressed device with ACK only, external burst requests, and byte operands. One spare SN74F04N gate in the existing floppy adapter converts active-high 82077AA DRQ to active-low REQ1. A 10 kohm pull-up on REQ1 and a 10 kohm pull-down on DRQ establish inactivity if either endpoint is absent. ACK1 connects to active-low DACK.

Add U_FDC_DATA, an SN74HCT245N, between FDC DB7..DB0 on its A port and system D7..D0 on its B port. Enable it for either a valid PIO FDC cycle or ACK1. Its direction and the FDC strobes reverse their PIO R/W interpretation during DMA. An SN74F10N and an SN74F08N join the existing adapter gates; Floppy Controller holds the package and pin allocation. 

FDC_DMA      = NOT ACK1_n
FDC_READ     = (FDC_PIO AND R/W) OR (FDC_DMA AND NOT R/W AND DTC_n)
FDC_WRITE    = (FDC_PIO AND NOT R/W) OR (FDC_DMA AND R/W AND DTC_n)
FDC_RD_n     = NOT FDC_READ
FDC_WR_n     = NOT FDC_WRITE
FDC_BUF_DIR  = (FDC_PIO AND R/W) OR (FDC_DMA AND NOT R/W)
FDC_BUF_OE_n = NOT (FDC_PIO OR FDC_DMA)

FDC_TC_n     = ACK1_n OR DONE_n OR DTC_n

Even physical bytes use UDS and the motherboard HIBYTE bridge even though the FDC is on D7..D0. Odd bytes use LDS directly, as manual section 4.3.2.3 describes. The TC equation produces an active-low pulse only when channel 1 is acknowledging its final operand and DTC proves that bus cycle succeeded. DTC is asserted in S8 of a single-address write, or S6 of a single-address read, and negates with ACK one state after the data strobes; the pulse therefore spans three states, 224.98 ns at the slowest DMA clock, entirely inside the DACK interval. That exceeds the 50 ns 82077AA terminal-count minimum. A failed cycle cannot assert TC. DTC_n also ends the FDC strobe while DACK is still asserted, so the controller sees the specified acknowledge hold and the DRAM data hold at the write edge.

Floppy DMA uses one unchained, physically contiguous command buffer. The BIOS uses a contiguous bounce buffer when user pages are not contiguous. A chained descriptor boundary would assert DONE before the command's final byte and is therefore forbidden for channel 1. Command and result phases remain PIO. Firmware enables the FIFO with threshold 8 and recovers or resets the command after an abort before freeing its pinned buffer.

14. Expansion Channels 2 and 3

Revision 2.2 of the connector contract changes five former ground contacts on each slot. Row b remains ground at all 32 positions.

Added per-slot DMA contacts
Contact Signal Direction at card
c26 CARD_DMA_REQ_n Open-collector output to 2.2 kohm motherboard pull-up
a29 CARD_DMA_ACK_n Motherboard output
c29 CARD_DMA_READY_n Open-collector output to 2.2 kohm motherboard pull-up
a32 CARD_DMA_DTC_n Motherboard output, qualified successful transfer
c32 CARD_DMA_DONE_n Motherboard output, qualified end of block 
CARD_DMA_DTC_n  = ACKx_n OR DTC_n
CARD_DMA_DONE_n = ACKx_n OR DONE_n

U_EXP_DMA_OR, an SN74F32N, supplies all four qualified outputs. Each acknowledge reaches its connector through the spare eighth channel of that slot's address-high HCT244, so no card pin touches a shared motherboard net. See Expansion Slots for the contact assignment and the card contract.

Cards use the lower system byte and an 8-bit ACK-and-READY protocol. During ACK, R/W describes memory: low tells the card to drive data for a device-to-memory transfer; high tells it to accept data. The card must present READY within 32 us and must hold request until ACK. It updates a FIFO or pointer only on DTC, not ACK. DONE marks the last transfer in the current descriptor. During descriptor fetches ACK is inactive, and an F00 and an F08 build the manual's Figure 4-12 circuit so PCL follows motherboard DTACK without involving the card.

15. Sequential Descriptors and Memory Copies

offset +0: MAR[31:16]  big-endian word
offset +2: MAR[15:0]   big-endian word
offset +4: MTCR        big-endian operand count
descriptor size: 6 bytes

BAR must be even and physical. BFCR and MFCR are $05. BTCR is the nonzero descriptor count. Each MTCR is nonzero and counts operands, not bytes. Descriptors and buffers remain pinned and supervisor-owned until completion or confirmed abort. Split arrays at 4 KiB frame boundaries and device protocol boundaries.

A descriptor reloads MAR and MTCR but not DAR. A dual-address memory copy therefore supports one scatter endpoint only. For two scattered endpoints, split the operation or use a contiguous bounce buffer. Word copies require even source and destination addresses. Forward overlapping copies count up when destination is below source; backward copies start at the last word and count both addresses down. Odd ends use CPU byte copies outside the DMA operation.

Copies use maximum-rate auto-request with a chunked operand count. GCR keeps its reset value and no channel uses limited-rate auto-request. The BIOS programs MTCR with one chunk, waits for the channel to finish, and reloads for the next chunk, so it sets both the processor stall per chunk and the spacing between chunks. 

word operand      = one read cycle + one write cycle
                  = 8 DMA clocks minimum, about 10 with DRAM service
chunk of 8 words  = 80 clocks = 12.0 us of processor denial
restart overhead  = register writes + 1.06 us post-START guard
copy rate at 100% duty = 2 bytes per 1.5 us = 1.33 MB/s
CPU MOVE.L loop        = 4 bytes per 2.0 us = 2.00 MB/s

The controller is slower than the processor at this job and always will be: a dual-address copy costs the same two bus cycles the CPU spends, at 6.6667 MHz instead of 10 MHz. The channel exists to move bytes while the processor does something else, at a bandwidth the BIOS chooses. Any copy the caller is going to wait for should run as a MOVE.L loop instead, and the BIOS service picks between the two.

16. Firmware Contract

  1. Accept DMA requests only through a BIOS call gate. Validate physical range, direction, permissions, alignment, operand size, counts, descriptor count, and device phase.
  2. Reject wrap past $3FFFFF, access below $020000 for a user owner, and every non-DRAM target.
  3. Pin each buffer and descriptor frame. Make descriptors immutable to the user. Record channel, owner, device operation, and cleanup action before START.
  4. Program MFCR and BFCR to supervisor data $05. Program DFCR to $05 for a memory-copy endpoint. Never use CPU-space $07.
  5. Abort stale state, load the complete configuration, clear CSR with $F6 or $FF, then write CCR as one byte. Do not access any DMAC register for seven full DMA clocks after START.
  6. Measure the guard against the slowest DMA clock, where seven periods are 1.0501 us, and enforce 1.10 us from the START write. Mask level 1 during the guard and make the handler defer register access until the saved deadline.
  7. Write SCR and CCR separately as bytes. Never start a new channel under external BEC halt. The hardware generates no halt or retry codes.
  8. Take the slot's DMA lock before borrowing its channel for a memory copy, and hold it until the slot's own configuration is restored. A card driver holds the same lock whenever it may raise a request.
  9. Program a memory copy one chunk at a time with maximum-rate auto-request. Pick the operand count from the processor stall the caller can accept, and space the chunks to set the bandwidth. Leave GCR at its reset value; no channel uses limited-rate auto-request.
  10. Copy on the processor when the caller waits for the result. A MOVE.L loop is faster than the controller, so the channel is only worth using when the processor has other work.
  11. On completion or error, stop device strobes, confirm ACT clear, recover the ATA/FDC/card protocol, release pins, then notify or terminate the recorded owner.

17. Timing, Latency, and Performance

DRAM and Refresh

The DRAM request detector uses shared AS, UDS/LDS, R/W, FC, and physical address signals, so it accepts either master. It samples the bank, lanes, address, and direction at request acceptance. Delayed write strobes do not start until READY permits UDS/LDS on a device-to-memory transfer. Refresh has priority at every legal cycle boundary and can run while the DMAC retains bus ownership. It does not wait for BGACK release.

A dual-address DMAC read latches data at the end of S6. The source may invalidate data no earlier than DTACK assertion under the manual's 150 ns maximum DTACK-to-data-invalid allowance. The HCT245 adds at most 28 ns and the DMAC requires 15 ns before its falling sample edge, leaving 107 ns for synchronization and board routing. The existing DRAM controller holds its output through AS/DS release, so it exceeds that interval. Verify the final transceiver output at DMAC pins.

Floppy Deadline

IDE or expansion timeout                         51.2 us
DMAC bus-error recovery, 25 clocks               3.75 us
request/arbitration minimum plus phase budget    3.00 us
one refresh and first DRAM service               1.50 us
board logic allowance                            2.00 us
conservative service bound                      61.45 us
82077 threshold-8 limit                         126.5 us
margin                                           65.05 us

The bound assumes no unbounded READY source. Expansion READY is limited to 32 us and motherboard timeout remains the final limit. The DMAC finishes an in-flight operand before changing channels; the 51.2 us line covers the longest such device cycle. Descriptor fetches complete in less than this timeout. The threshold-8 FIFO therefore retains more than 65 us of margin at 500 kbit/s.

Bus Denial

IDE and expansion activations are limited to 32 operands. With the conservative 1.8 us IDE device-to-memory word interval, a chunk holds the bus for at most 57.6 us plus arbitration and one refresh. A timed out device aborts sooner than that bound. A memory-copy chunk holds the bus for its programmed operand count, 12.0 us for the eight-word default, plus arbitration, one refresh, and the release phase. Floppy releases the bus whenever DRQ removes its burst request. Every figure here is processor denial; a higher-priority channel preempts a lower one at the next operand boundary, so no device waits for a whole chunk.

Direction-Specific IDE Rate

QE makes READY 0.80 to 1.00 us after the asynchronous cycle start. A memory-to-device read can then finish after the DMAC READY/DTACK synchronizers, yielding 1.10 to 1.40 us per word before refresh, or 1.43 to 1.82 MB/s. A device-to-memory write adds READY-controlled data strobes and DRAM write service, yielding 1.35 to 1.80 us per word, or 1.11 to 1.48 MB/s. Command issue, status checks, arbitration, refresh, and 32-word chunk restarts reduce end-to-end throughput.

PIO Comparison

A representative PIO word loop uses a word read from the ATA data register, a word write to DRAM, pointer update, count/branch work, and instruction fetches. Even if each bus operation took only one 400 ns CPU cycle, the data read and store alone consume 800 ns and the loop necessarily consumes more cycles for code and control. DMA performs one memory bus cycle per IDE word after the device provides the word; the CPU cannot fetch while DMA owns the bus but can run between the bounded chunks. This comparison establishes reduced CPU bus work, not a guaranteed disk rate. Floppy DMA reduces CPU service work without changing the media's 500 kbit/s transfer rate.

18. Electrical, Fanout, and Bias

Required idle bias
Signals Bias Reason
BR_n, BGACK_n, OWN_n, IRQ_n 2.2 kohm to +5 V Open-drain release with bounded rise time
DONE_n 1.5 kohm to +5 V Shared open-drain line; about 3.0 mA at VOL=0.5 V, below the 8.9 mA sink rating
AS_n, UDS_n, LDS_n, R/W, DTC_n, UAS_n, DBEN_n, DDIR, HIBYTE_n 10 kohm to +5 V Inactive state during three-state handoff
FC2..FC0 10 kohm to +5 V Defined handoff level and A84G item 1
REQ0_n, PCL1_n 4.7 kohm to +5 V Unused request and ACK-only PCL inactive
REQ2_n, REQ3_n and both CARD_DMA_READY_n contacts 2.2 kohm to +5 V Expansion open-collector card outputs. PCL2_n and PCL3_n come from an F08 and need no bias.

A 1.5 kohm DONE pull-up and a conservative 50 pF node cross 2.0 V in about 30 ns. A 10 kohm part would take about 203 ns and is rejected. The 2.2 kohm BR/BGACK/OWN pull-ups take about 45 ns at 50 pF and draw about 2.05 mA at VOL=0.5 V, below the DMAC 5.3 mA bus-control sink rating. IRQ draws the same resistor current plus the LS148 input and remains below its 8.9 mA rating.

Each CPU A1..A7 line gains one 15 pF maximum DMAC input. A8..A23 gain one disabled ACT373 output, budgeted at 10 pF because the TI sheet gives leakage but no output capacitance maximum. FC0..FC2 gain one 15 pF DMAC pin and a pull-up. Replacing the CPU with the ACT373 as master does not add receiver loads; it changes the driver. The ACT373 guarantees 24 mA drive and 9.5 ns data-to-Q maximum at 5 V into 50 pF, stronger and faster than the CPU for the existing decoder load.

The previously tight CPU R/W estimate was 86 pF. It gains the 15 pF DMAC pin and one 10 pF HIBYTE direction input, totaling 111 pF before routes, above the former 100 pF planning target. Add U_DMA_CTRL_BUF, a CD74ACT244E: CPU/DMAC R/W, AS, UDS, LDS, and FC feed one local receiver each, and the buffer drives motherboard consumers. Its outputs are disabled only during reset handoff, not by ownership, because the selected master already drives the shared inputs. This removes the former direct fanout and restores each master pin below 50 pF known load. Recalculate series damping after route extraction.

MASTER_CLK_40 now drives three F74 clock inputs instead of one. The F74 sheet omits input capacitance. Reserve 10 pF per input as an engineering ceiling and 10 pF for the short star routes, sockets, and probe, totaling 40 pF against the oscillator's 50 pF load condition. This is not a datasheet proof. Measure the three loaded clock pins; fit separate source resistors if ringing crosses the F74 thresholds.

19. Power and Thermal Limits

Reserve the manual's full 2.0 W MC68450 dissipation at 25 C and 8 MHz because no lower-frequency figure is supplied. Add 0.8 W for the three FAST divider packages. The remaining logic is fourteen ACT and HCT packages, seven more FAST packages, and one PALCE16V8Q. At 15 mA for each CMOS package, 15 mA for each FAST package, and the quarter-power PAL's own 55 mA, that group draws 0.37 A and dissipates 1.85 W.

+5 V reservation for the DMA addition
Group Current Power
MC68450L8 at its rated maximum 0.40 A 2.0 W
Two SN74F74N and one SN74F02N divider 0.16 A 0.8 W
Demultiplex, isolation, buffer, glue, and interlocks 0.37 A 1.85 W
Total 0.93 A 4.65 W

The existing 5 A supply budget must retain that headroom after every board load is summed. The current figures are catalogue maximums for the families rather than measured values; confirm them on the assembled board.

The ceramic package has estimated theta-JA 30 C/W and theta-JC 15 C/W. At 2.0 W, the still-air junction-rise estimate is 60 C. The manual specifies 0 C through 70 C ambient but gives no operating maximum junction temperature. The 150 C storage limit is not an operating limit. Forced airflow is required, but no unquantified credit is used in the design proof. Measure local ambient and case temperature at maximum traffic, calculate junction rise from the measured case with theta-JC, and obtain an applicable Motorola junction limit before declaring the thermal check closed.

20. Layout and Decoupling

  • Use four layers at minimum with uninterrupted ground beneath the DMAC, demultiplexers, divider, and bus routes. Six layers are permitted.
  • Place both ACT373 latches and both DMAC data HCT245s beside pins 33..48. Keep each multiplexed stub short.
  • Place the HIBYTE transceiver where the two byte lanes meet. Match each crossed path and avoid a loop around the CPU socket.
  • Place both F74 state sections and their F02 feedback gates together. Route MASTER_CLK_40 as a short three-branch star with individual resistor footprints.
  • Fit 100 nF at every logic package and both MC68450 supply pairs. Fit 1 uF beside the MC68450 and each group of four glue packages.
  • Keep BR, BG, BGACK, OWN, BEC, DTACK, and IRQ away from oscillator and ATA cable routes. Put pull-ups at the receiving cluster.
  • Provide labeled test points for DMA_CLK, BR, BG, BGACK, OWN, AS, DTACK at both sides of isolation, BEC0..2, IRQ, every REQ/ACK pair, DTC, and DONE.

21. A84G Errata Applicability

Five items are honoured by construction and five are avoided because the board never enters the case they describe. Three of the avoided ones, items 4, 8, and 9, apply only to limited-rate auto-request. Dropping LRAR was not a convenience: item 8 requires the burst to cover a whole processor cycle, the largest burst the part offers is 17.325 us of processor cycle, and this board has two cycles that can exceed it. A CL-GD5428 display-memory access holds IOCHRDY low for as long as screen refresh needs, and an unanswered address runs to the 51.2 us bus timeout. Neither is schedulable, so the item could not be satisfied and memory copies use maximum-rate auto-request with a chunked operand count instead.

MC68450AD A84G restrictions
Item Applies Design rule
1 Yes FC lines are used and also have 10 kohm pull-ups for idle handoff.
2 Avoided No relinquish-and-retry BEC code is generated.
3 Yes Direct M68000 arbitration is used. DMAC CS is ownership-qualified, so CPU CS cannot overlap DMA ownership.
4 Avoided The restriction applies only while a channel runs LRAR. No channel does. The borrowed copy channel still takes priority 3, below every device channel, so the documented workaround holds if LRAR is ever revisited.
5 Yes No register access for seven clocks after STR. Seven periods of the slowest DMA clock is 1.0501 us, so firmware enforces 1.10 us and defers level-1 service.
6 Avoided Firmware never starts a channel under external BEC halt; hardware emits no halt.
7 Avoided DMAC IACK is tied high. The motherboard supplies level-1 autovector.
8 Avoided No channel uses LRAR. The board cannot satisfy this item, which is why: the largest burst Table 5-3 offers is 128 clocks, so the longest permitted processor cycle is 128 - 12.5 = 115.5 clocks, or 17.325 us. A CL-GD5428 display-memory access holds IOCHRDY low for as long as screen refresh needs, and an unanswered cycle runs to the 51.2 us bus timeout. Neither can be scheduled away.
9 Avoided The restriction applies only while a channel runs LRAR. The BGACK qualification on DMA fault capture is kept regardless, and reset still bypasses ownership and has priority.
10 Yes SCR and CCR are always separate byte writes.

22. Implementation Checklist

Pre-layout and board checks
Check State and pass condition
Document logic review Complete: channel assignment, mux polarity, DTACK isolation, BEC codes, interrupt, and connector contacts are fixed.
Divider equations Complete by truth table. Bench simulation and scope startup remain board checks.
PAL feasibility Equations stay within eight outputs and the stated product-term limits. A compatible CUPL fitter is not installed; JEDEC fit and checksum remain a build check.
Bus handoff Scope all twelve relative CPU/DMA phase positions. No master may drive before the other releases; OWN must lead and lag BGACK as documented.
Register access Test every byte lane, word/long register, mirror rejection policy, post-STR guard, and reset value.
IDE Measure both DMA directions at connector pins for address setup, strobe width, data setup/hold, IORDY wait, recovery, 32-word restart, timeout, and abort.
Floppy Test even and odd byte DMA, FIFO threshold 8, DACK/TC overlap, suppressed DTC, abort recovery, and bounce buffers.
Descriptors Test aligned arrays, 4 KiB splits, final DONE, descriptor fault, zero counts, and pinned-frame rejection.
Refresh Run maximum IDE and copy traffic. Every pending refresh must start at the next legal DRAM boundary without waiting for bus release.
Late fault Inject page, protection, timeout, and descriptor faults around DTACK. BEC must remain stable for two clocks and no failed cycle may assert DTC.
DMA range interlock Program a channel with an address in each of I/O space, the VGA aperture, an expansion window, the page-table aperture, and the ROM. Every one must abort with no select asserted at the target and no page-table entry disturbed.
Boot overlay With the overlay enabled, a DMA read of physical $000000 returns DRAM, not firmware.
Loading Extract capacitance, include sockets and probe, verify clock phases and bus rise times, then select damping resistors.
Thermal Measure MC68450 case and local ambient under maximum traffic and close the junction-limit check from manufacturer data.
